Ordnance 0.4.2. Automatic downloads, and mods that used to refuse to install.

## What's new

**Automatic downloading (opt-in).** With automatic update checks on, you can now also have Ordnance download and install updates it can fetch itself — GitHub, GameBanana, and ModWorkshop — right after a check finds them, no per-mod click. It's a separate toggle in Settings, off by default, and it never touches Nexus Mods (those still go through the browser).

**Mods that wouldn't install now do.** A lot of hand-written manifest.json files use a non-UUID "Guid" (like `r40_cs_awp_combo_v2`) or omit the field entirely. Ordnance used to reject both. It now turns a slug into a stable UUID (same slug, same identity across reinstalls) and gives a manifest with no Guid a local identity, so those mods install instead of erroring out.

**The native file picker is actually fixed.** The "Add" button now opens your real desktop file dialog on Linux, not the goofy breadcrumb window. (This landed after 0.4.1 was tagged, so 0.4.1 didn't have it.)

**Deploy errors name the culprit.** When a stat-plan deploy fails, the error now says which mod caused it and offers copy-to-clipboard / report buttons instead of a bare stack trace.

**Smaller fixes.** Mod source link sits beside the version tag; updating a mod no longer auto-adds it to the active profile; toggle switches line up in one column for Legacy mods; the AyakaMods provider docs are corrected.

## What Ordnance does

**Import from your current mod manager.** One-click import from HD2 Arsenal and Echelon — plus the older HD2 mod manager, Vortex, and your Downloads folder, with names, on/off state, and options intact.

**Automatic update checking and (optionally) downloading.** Ordnance checks every mod against its source — AyakaMods, GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and Nexus Mods — and, when you enable it, downloads and installs the ones it can fetch itself.

**One deploy, everything enabled.** Merge mods and generated stat-plan edits into a single sealed swap and a single boot script. No per-mod loader conflicts.

## Get it

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `Ordnance-0.4.2-windows-x64.exe` |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | `Ordnance-0.4.2-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `Ordnance-0.4.2-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

**Browser extension:** `ordnance-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip` or `ordnance-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip`. Load it unpacked. The button says Install with Ordnance.
